Traditional Sugar Skulls

Served at: Dia de los Angelitos · Dia de los Muertos

Makes about 12 medium skullsPrep 30 min

Sugar Skulls are colorful, decorative confections made from sugar and are a quintessential part of Dia de los Angelitos and Dia de los Muertos celebrations. These skulls honor deceased loved ones and are often personalized with names and vibrant designs, symbolizing the sweetness of life and the remembrance of those who have passed.

Ingredients

  • 3 cups granulated sugar (600 g)
  • 3 tablespoons meringue powder
  • 3 tablespoons water
  • Food coloring gels (various colors)
  • Decorative icing tubes or piping bags
  • Foil skull molds or plastic skull molds

Method

  1. In a large mixing bowl, combine the granulated sugar and meringue powder.
  2. Add water gradually and mix with your hands until the mixture holds together like wet sand.
  3. Press the sugar mixture firmly into the skull molds, packing tightly to avoid cracks.
  4. Carefully remove the molded sugar skulls from the molds and place them on a flat surface to dry.
  5. Allow the skulls to dry and harden for at least 24 hours in a dry area.
  6. Once dry, use colored icing tubes or piping bags filled with colored icing to decorate the skulls with traditional patterns and names.

Tips

  • Ensure the mixture is tightly packed in the molds to prevent crumbling when dry.
  • Use meringue powder instead of egg whites for food safety and longer shelf life.
  • If you don’t have molds, you can shape the sugar mixture by hand or use cookie cutters.
